candidates.evidence: Noah called upon God (نادى) and God responded (استجبنا); explicit Noah context in both
Both say Noah and family saved (نجيناه وأهله) from great distress (الكرب العظيم); nearly exact Arabic phrase
Both recount drowning of Noah's rejecting people (أغرقنا / أغرقنا الذين كذبوا)
Both Abraham addressing father and people (لأبيه وقومه) challenging their objects of worship
Abraham challenges worship of carved objects versus statues; distinct lines of same idol-confrontation narrative
Abraham's people order burning (حرقوه / ألقوه في الجحيم); 29:24 adds rescue
Near-parallel wording: وأرادوا به كيدا فجعلناهم... (plot against Abraham and failed scheme)
Both explicitly announce Isaac (بشرناه بإسحاق / فبشرناها بإسحاق); 11:71 concerns Sarah and adds Jacob
كذلك نجزي المحسنين appears in both (37:105 with إنا prefix)
وتركنا عليه في الآخرين identical in both, concerning different prophets
في الآخرين common; Abraham's prayer for enduring favorable mention and its fulfillment in 37:108
سلام على ... parallel blessings on Abraham versus Moses and Aaron, not same episode

existing_flags.evidence: 37:104 calls Abraham in the sacrifice narrative (يا إبراهيم); 21:90 answers Zechariah's prayer and grants John (يحيى). No same speaker, event, or distinctive lexical parallel. Both contain general calling/answering motifs only.
existing_flags.recommendation: quarantine for editorial review; do not delete before provenance and reversible backup

existing_flags.evidence: 37:109 سلام على إبراهيم (peace upon Abraham); 19:57 ورفعناه مكانا عليا (raising Idris to a high station). Neither same person nor shared formula; link appears unrelated.
existing_flags.recommendation: quarantine for editorial review; do not delete before provenance and reversible backup

other_existing.evidence: Both explicitly describe Abraham's opponents ordering him burned.

contextual_hold.reason: 51:28 mentions unnamed learned boy; 11:71 explicitly names Isaac; scholarly identification and narrative differences require further work.

interpretive_caution: 37:101–107 sacrifice narrative does not name the boy. Do not assert Ishmael or Isaac as explicit Qur'anic identification. Cross-reference to 11:71 or 51:28 should not be presented as proof of the unnamed boy's identity.
